# LIBCOB porting parity — typed C↔Rust symbol map

> Produced by `gnucobol-rs-port-index` (PORT-INDEX.1): the admitted libcob C is parsed into a
> symbol index with **preprocessor status** (compiled / `#if 0` / config-gated), the Rust port is
> parsed into a **real-`fn`** index (comment/string-aware), and the two are joined. A C function
> counts as ported only when a real Rust `fn` of that name exists — a name appearing solely in a
> doc comment is a **doc-only false hit**, not a port. **Byte** parity is proven separately by the
> per-court oracle sweeps in `lab/verify-sealed-courts.sh`.

Column meanings: **source** = function definitions in the `.c`; **compiled** = reached by the
preprocessor in the admitted build; **disabled** = `#if 0`/config-gated source mirrors;
**active/inactive/test** = real Rust `fn` counterpart kinds; **doc-only** = name only in a
comment (false hit, NOT a port); **missing** = absent; **active parity** = compiled fns with a
real Rust `fn` (active / inactive mirror / test). This is *symbol* parity, not behaviour parity —
oracle-backed *byte* parity is the separate per-court sweeps.

## Gaps — compiled C functions with no real Rust `fn`

None. Every compiled libcob function across all files has a real Rust counterpart.

## How this is produced (reproducible)

`cargo run -p gnucobol-rs-port-index -- parity` joins two machine indexes under
`reports/port-index/` (`libcob-symbols.json`, `rust-symbols.json`, `parity-detailed.json`).
`-- check` is the anti-staleness gate (regenerate-and-diff). The C-side compiled set is
cross-checked by the doxygen parse (`DOXYGEN-PARITY.md`).
